title: Two elders from nomadic Dewasi community seated on a wooden charpai in the rural countryside of District - Pali, Rajasthan.jpg
author: Jagdish dewasi 10
description: Two elderly men belonging to the Dewasi community sit on a traditional charpai (woven cot) outside a rural dwelling in Village Sowaniya, Pali district, Rajasthan, India. Both men wear bright yellow turbans, a distinctive element of traditional attire in the region, often symbolizing identity, honor, and protection from the harsh desert climate. The Dewasi community of western Rajasthan is traditionally associated with pastoral and agrarian livelihoods. Members of this community are known for livestock rearing—especially sheep, goats, and camels—as well as large-scale farming. Their lifestyle is closely connected with the semi-arid landscape of Rajasthan, where animal husbandry, seasonal grazing, and village agriculture remain important aspects of everyday life. The charpai on which the elders are seated is a common piece of furniture across rural South Asia. In village settings, it functions not only as a resting place but also as a social gathering space where elders converse, share stories, and discuss matters related to community life. In the background, stacks of harvested crop residue and mud-plastered village structures illustrate the agrarian environment typical of villages in Pali district. This image documents elements of Dewasi cultural identity, including traditional clothing, rural architecture, and the enduring village lifestyle of western Rajasthan.
